title: A2 checkpoint
can: Hold a full conversation with a stranger, then check your level.
doneText: That's the end of A2. Anything you missed is now in your weak spots, ready to review.

discover.intro: The same questions, asked two ways. One way is for a friend, the other for a stranger.
discover.question: What changes when you talk to a stranger?
options: The verb takes the él and ella form (es, hace, ha), and you can add usted.
You add por favor to every question.
Nothing: Spanish uses the same words for everyone.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Compare eres with es, haces with hace, and has with ha.
discover.reveal: With usted, every verb you know takes the él and ella form. That works in every tense you've met. Here is the whole course in one conversation:

blocks.text: This chapter mixes everything from chapters 1 to 11. Each mistake goes to the weak spot it belongs to, so after it you'll know exactly what to review.
With people around your own age, Spaniards move to tú very quickly, often straight away. Use usted with older people, officials and in formal places, and follow their lead.

blocks.title: Keep it going
blocks.note: The easiest way to keep a conversation going: answer, then turn the question back.

blocks.title: Conversation savers

blocks.text: CEFR A2 means you can handle short everyday conversations: introducing yourself, ordering, shopping, directions, plans and what you've done. If you've got this far, that's you.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Write a message to someone you met on the train: who you are, what you've done on your trip, what you like, and your plans for tomorrow.
write.starter: Hola, soy {name}. Soy de…  He visitado…  Me gusta…  Mañana voy a…
write.model: Hola, soy {name}. Soy de Inglaterra y estoy de viaje por España. Esta semana he visitado Granada y Sevilla. Me gusta mucho la comida, sobre todo las tapas. Creo que Sevilla es la ciudad más bonita. Mañana voy a visitar Córdoba. ¿Y tú?
checklist: Ser for who you are, estar for where you are
He visitado for this week, voy a for tomorrow
Me gusta, and an opinion with creo que

boss.title: On the train to Sevilla
boss.persona: You are Manuel, a friendly retired teacher from Sevilla, sitting next to the learner on the AVE train from Madrid. Start with usted, and switch to tú if the learner suggests it. Chat about where they are from, their trip so far, what they like and their plans. This is the A2 checkpoint: use the present, ir a + verb, gustar and the pretérito perfecto, but keep each reply short and simple. Speak European Spanish.

turns.en: Good afternoon. Are you from here?
choices: No, soy de Inglaterra. Estoy de viaje.
No, estoy de Inglaterra. Soy de viaje.
Where you're from takes ser: soy de Inglaterra. A trip takes estar: estoy de viaje.
No, es de Inglaterra. Está de viaje.
Es and está are he, she or usted. About yourself: soy, estoy.

turns.npc: ¡Qué bien! ¿Y qué ha visitado en España?
turns.en: How lovely! And what have you visited in Spain?
choices: He visitado Madrid y Granada.
Ha visitado Madrid y Granada.
Ha is he, she or usted. About yourself: he visitado.
He visitada Madrid y Granada.
The -ado form never changes: visitado.

turns.en: And do you like Spanish food?
choices: Sí, me gusta mucho, sobre todo las tapas.
Sí, me gustan mucho la comida.
One thing, la comida: me gusta.
Sí, le gusta mucho, sobre todo las tapas.
Le gusta is he, she or usted. About yourself: me gusta.

turns.npc: ¿Y qué va a hacer en Sevilla?
turns.en: And what are you going to do in Seville?
choices: Voy a ver la catedral y a comer tapas.
Voy ver la catedral y comer tapas.
Plans need the a: voy a ver.
Va a ver la catedral y a comer tapas.
Va is he, she or usted. About yourself: voy a.

boss.closing: ¡Muy bien! Su español es muy bueno. ¡Disfrute de Sevilla!
boss.closingEn: Very good! Your Spanish is very good. Enjoy Seville!
boss.chatOpeningEn: By the way, shall we use tú with each other?
